title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Asian shares fell Monday on weak Japan GDP and China data; chipmakers led losses, with SK Hynix sliding over 6% on Nvidia/export-curb worries, and US futures gave back early gains ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's speech.

Markets: Brent crude dipped below $90/barrel (lowest since August) after the IEA flagged a Q4 oil surplus and on easing Iran tensions; gold slid below $3,900/oz on dollar strength and rising Fed rate-hike bets.
Companies: Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday, a closely watched print after a rough stretch for AI and chip stocks across Asia and the US.
Macro/Policy: CME FedWatch now prices roughly 94% odds of a 25bp rate hike in December; KC Fed President Schmid said inflation is still 'running too hot.'
Macro/Policy: October FOMC meeting minutes are due Wednesday, with markets looking for confirmation of the Fed's hawkish tilt.
